decisions.summary: This feature itself owes no settlement-review (tooling only, no manifest moves); _review_owed.py decides.
decisions.why: The request is about the review tooling; nothing on a map changes. Consistent with FR-005/231 and with the request's own subject.

decisions.summary: Verification is make hooks-test plus make quick; the gate is not re-keyed; lands DIRECT.
decisions.why: SC-005 says lands DIRECT (guard scripts and tooling tests, no engine code); nothing in the request asks for more.

decisions.summary: New branches are added as functions inside pair-hooks.sh (503 lines) and test-pair-hooks.sh (335), no split; _review_owed.py gains one lifted function tested over plain text.
decisions.why: A file-shape choice inside the 1,000-line rule; the spec does not settle it and the request does not touch it.

decisions.summary: _review_snapshot.py writes dispatch.md per map from one template, the engine key passed in with --key, the path printed on the map's line; verify and the permit branch print N agents one per map in this same message.
decisions.why: Implements FR-002 exactly (the location, the contents, the N-files instruction); the request's 'make the correct thing happen automatically' is served, nothing narrowed.

decisions.summary: maps_named(prompt, all_pool_maps) lifted into _review_prereq.py; names from _review_owed.pool_map_names(root) over both pool trees; snapshot directories first, bare-name words second.
decisions.why: FR-001 and D2 verbatim: counted against EVERY pool map, not the owed set, which is what closes the shape the GM named for an unowed or legacy map.

decisions.summary: Two or more maps: refuse with exit 2 before the prerequisite check, rule review-multi-map, no escape token.
decisions.why: The GM: 'could we refuse a map review before it happens if the review asks for a review of more than 1 map?' - yes, and D1's no-escape is the spec's. Not a narrowing; it is the literal thing.

decisions.summary: One map: after the existing rules permit, write_pairing a dispatched record {map: {key, at}} and log review-dispatched.
decisions.why: FR-003's 'at each permitted settlement-review dispatch the guard records'. Implementer's note, not a finding: 'the existing rules permit' includes the PAIR_OK-in-prompt escape path, which exits before the gate check today - the record must be written on that path too or FR-003's dispatch-counting misses an escaped review.

decisions.summary: When every owed map has a dispatch at this key, compute the span and log reviews-parallel or reviews-serialized; never refuse.
decisions.why: FR-004 and D4; research R3 states why it cannot be forced. The GM asked for parallelization to be folded in; the plan folds in what a hook can guarantee and measures the rest, which is the spec's stated shape.

decisions.summary: Stop branch: missing set = owed minus recorded-at-key minus dispatched-at-key minus pending-agent-naming-it (transcript grep); placed after review_recorded and before the half-open refusal; quiet when review_pending holds and the set is empty; refused once per (key, sorted set) via stop_missing_told, rule review-map-undispatched, naming the maps and their dispatch.md.
decisions.why: FR-003 exactly; review_recorded is already all-maps (_review_prereq.recorded), so nothing short-circuits it. Implementer's note, not a narrowing: the plan's placement range admits a position BEFORE review_waived, and FR-003 says PAIR_OK on the gate clears the rule - the check must sit after review_waived (or honor waived_key inside), else a waived turn is refused for missing maps.

decisions.summary: rendering_only(tasks_text) -> int|None, the task regex copied from tests/test_task_research_boxes.py with a pointer because a guard cannot import a test module.
decisions.why: A mechanism for FR-005; the classification vocabulary is the project's existing one (R4).

decisions.summary: active_features(root, base) = the pointer's directory plus every specs/*/ directory the delta against the base touches that has a tasks.md, ticked or not (the in-progress rule's derivation widened: at push no box is open); an empty set OWES.
decisions.why: RE-REVIEWED THIS ROUND (the one changed passage; the digest moved from 7ea83247 to c3976141, confirmed by git diff 5764fd0a..18b3bd95, which touches only this bullet). Reviewer note: this review ran on the session's model rather than Opus, the Opus weekly limit having been reached, by the session's decision. Ruling: the bullet is the amended FR-005/D7 verbatim - the pointer's feature AND every delta-touched feature directory with a tasks.md, open box or not, conjunction for the waiver, empty set owes. Against the request: the GM asked to skip the review 'for features like this one specifically, i.e. changing a glyph rendering convention' and said 'Yes to both' to a waiver keyed on the task classification; the plan keys it on the classification of the feature set the project already derives for 'the feature this push is' (feature 133, derived not declared, so a pointer cannot evade it), and the widening can only OWE a review, never skip one the GM would have run - so it does not carve out any case the GM asked to have skipped, and it serves the GM's stated purpose that the tooling makes the correct thing happen without anyone remembering. The one cost, stated: a rendering-only feature whose delta also touches another feature's specs/ directory (a cross-feature docs edit) owes a review the GM's words alone would skip; that errs toward a review, not away from one. The empty-set-owes clause, an implementer's note in the previous record, is now in the plan's text and matches FR-005. Note: the spec's FR-005 amendment is concurrently under a MODE 3 verify round; this ruling is against the request and the amended text, and holds on either outcome of that round because the plan says what the amended text says.

decisions.summary: changed_maps returns no names with the reason 'rendering-only feature(s) <dirs>: <n> task(s) all research: rendering, no settlement-review owed (feature 248)' when every derived feature is rendering-only; --why prints it; --maps callers unchanged.
decisions.why: FR-005's waiver, reaching every decision point through the one script. 'Every derived feature' now reads with the plan's own 'an empty set OWES' clause, so the previous record's implementer's note on the vacuous case is answered in the plan text.

decisions.summary: review-gate.sh section 2 per changed manifest: PASS/NEEDS-WORK at the pushed tree's engine key (make -s engine-key REF=worktree, once) passes; else the rendering waiver passes (recorded escaped-class review-waived-rendering); else no record at all plus a notes touch passes; else refuse naming which, rules map-stale-verdict / map-not-reviewable / map-no-review.
decisions.why: FR-006 and D5 exactly; the three passes and three refusals match FR-008 and SC-004 as amended at round 3. Serves the GM's first message (the notes-touch redundancy was the 1.5 minutes). Implementer's note, not a finding: 'the pushed tree' is HEAD, and REF=worktree equals it only on a clean tree - the push procedure's own clean-tree requirement is what makes the two the same key.

decisions.summary: The parallel/serialized proof uses an injected clock PAIR_NOW, honored in a fixture only.
decisions.why: SC-002's 'fixture-clock minute'; the seams-only-in-a-fixture pattern the idle-tests guard already uses.

decisions.summary: _hookdeps unchanged because the suites already carry these scripts; the new rule slugs get rows in test_guard_firing_log.py.
decisions.why: FR-008's 'the firing-log census sees every new rule'; whether _hookdeps really needs no change is verified at implementation, not a fidelity matter.

decisions.summary: settlement-review.md gains the one-map rule and the prompt files; CLAUDE.md's pair row the four rules and the waiver; dev/reviews.md the doctrine; review-ledger.md unchanged.
decisions.why: FR-007 verbatim, and the ledger row-per-pass stays by-hand as the spec's Out of scope says.
